## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Cūḷantaraduka* ("Shorter Intermediate Set of Dyads") is a section of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and final treatise of the Theravāda *Abhidhamma Piṭaka* [SuttaCentral]. In the formal structure of the Abhidhamma matrix (*mātikā*), the *cūḷantaraduka* comprises a set of seven dyads covering various pairs of factors (such as conditioned and unconditioned states), functioning alongside the *mahantaraduka* and *piṭṭhiduka* as intermediate dyadic groupings distinct from the corruption-oriented clusters (*gocchaka*) [Potter 1996]. In this specific section of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the system of conditional relations (*paccaya*) is systematically applied to the categories of the *cūḷantaraduka* [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].

Secondary literature does not treat this section of the *Paṭṭhāna* independently; references to the *cūḷantaraduka* in modern scholarship instead address the dyad matrix as it appears in the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the *Dhātukathā*, and comparative Abhidhamma taxonomy [Potter 1996].

According to DharmaNexus, the text exhibits 755 internal text-reuse matches across 149 Pali canonical texts, reflecting the standardized formulaic exposition characteristic of the *Paṭṭhāna* [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial structural parallels occur with other chapters of the *Paṭṭhāna*, notably the *Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 20.8; 32 matches, sharing up to 6,251 characters), the *Hetuduka* (Patthana 6.1; 30 matches), another analytical treatment of the *Cūḷantaraduka* (Patthana 2.2; 23 matches), and the *Mahantaraduka* (Patthana 20.5; 20 matches) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records 5 low-level matches with the Tibetan *Mahāvyutpatti* (D4346, best plausibility score 15) [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral does not record any standalone translations or curated external parallels for this section [SuttaCentral].
